Participants disagree about responsibility: US envoy Dennis Ross and Israeli negotiator Shlomo Ben-Ami largely blamed Arafat, while US official Robert Malley and Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat argued Israel's offer was less generous than portrayed.

title: Second (Al-Aqsa) Intifada begins
summary: Opposition leader Ariel Sharon's visit to the Temple Mount/Haram al-Sharif on 28 September 2000 was followed the next day by protests in which Israeli police used lethal force, and by a spiral of uprising, armed attacks and suicide bombings, and Israeli military operations. The Mitchell Report found the visit did not cause the intifada but was poorly timed, and faulted both sides. B'Tselem counts, for September 2000 to September 2010 (a period that also includes the 2008–09 Gaza war), 6,371 Palestinians killed by Israeli security forces (at least 2,996 of them not taking part in hostilities) and 1,083 Israelis killed by Palestinians (741 civilians).

title: October 2000 events: Arab citizens killed in protests
summary: In early October 2000 protests by Arab citizens in the Galilee and Wadi Ara spread into clashes; police killed 13 Palestinian Arabs, 12 of them citizens of Israel and one a resident of Gaza. The Or Commission (appointed November 2000, reported September 2003) found police gunfire unjustified and the use of snipers illegal; no officer was indicted.

title: Rocket fire from Gaza on Sderot
summary: From 2001, early in the second intifada, militants in the Gaza Strip began firing home-made Qassam rockets and mortars at Sderot and nearby communities; rockets killed 13 people in Sderot by 2008.

title: Sharon elected prime minister
summary: In a special election for prime minister only, Ariel Sharon (Likud) defeated incumbent Ehud Barak by 62.5% to 37.5% amid the intifada.

title: Dolphinarium discotheque bombing
summary: A suicide bomber blew himself up in a queue of young people outside the Dolphinarium discotheque on the Tel Aviv seafront, killing 21. Islamic Jihad first claimed the attack; Hamas later said it was responsible.

title: Minister Rehavam Ze'evi assassinated
summary: Tourism Minister Rehavam Ze'evi was shot dead in the Hyatt hotel in Jerusalem by a Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine cell, which presented it as retaliation for Israel's killing of PFLP leader Abu Ali Mustafa in August 2001.

title: Karine A arms ship seized
summary: Israeli naval commandos boarded the freighter Karine A in the Red Sea without a shot, finding about 50 tons of weapons including Katyusha rockets, anti-tank missiles and explosives; Israel said the Iranian-supplied cargo was bound for the Palestinian Authority, which denied involvement.

title: Park Hotel Passover bombing, Netanya
summary: A Hamas suicide bomber attacked a Passover seder for about 250 guests at the Park Hotel in Netanya, killing 30 civilians (Israeli MFA; HRW gives 29) and injuring 143.

title: Arab Peace Initiative
summary: The Arab League summit in Beirut adopted a Saudi-inspired plan offering normal relations with Israel in the context of a comprehensive peace, in return for full withdrawal from territories occupied since June 1967, a Palestinian state with East Jerusalem as its capital, and a 'just solution' to the refugee problem in accordance with UN General Assembly resolution 194.

title: Operation Defensive Shield
summary: Two days after the Netanya bombing Israel launched a major West Bank operation, re-entering Area A cities including Ramallah, Nablus, Bethlehem, Tulkarm, Qalqilya and Jenin. In the battle of Jenin refugee camp 52–53 Palestinians were killed—at least 22 of them civilians according to Human Rights Watch, up to half according to the UN—and 23 Israeli soldiers. Palestinian officials' claims of a massacre of hundreds were not borne out by HRW or the UN, though HRW documented unlawful killings and use of human shields. The IDF declared the operation over on 21 April.

title: Construction of the West Bank barrier approved
summary: Israel's cabinet approved the first phase of a barrier of fences, walls and patrol roads in and along the West Bank (Government Decision 2077), presented as a means to stop suicide bombers. Much of its route ran inside the West Bank, around settlement blocs and East Jerusalem, separating many Palestinian communities from land and services.

title: Nobel economics prize to Daniel Kahneman
summary: Israeli-American psychologist Daniel Kahneman shared the 2002 economics prize with Vernon Smith for integrating psychological research on judgement and decision-making into economics.

title: Election to the 16th Knesset
summary: Under the restored parliamentary system, Sharon's Likud won 38 seats, Labor 19 and the secularist Shinui 15; Sharon remained prime minister.

title: Ilan Ramon killed in Columbia disaster
summary: Colonel Ilan Ramon, an Israeli Air Force pilot and Israel's first astronaut, died with his six crewmates when Space Shuttle Columbia broke apart during re-entry at the end of the STS-107 mission.

title: Quartet 'Road Map' presented
summary: The Quartet (US, EU, UN, Russia) presented Israel and the Palestinian Authority with a performance-based, three-phase plan toward a permanent two-state settlement by 2005, requiring an end to Palestinian violence and a freeze on settlement activity.

title: Tel Aviv's White City listed by UNESCO
title_he: העיר הלבנה בתל אביב מוכרזת אתר מורשת עולמית
summary: UNESCO inscribed the 'White City of Tel-Aviv – the Modern Movement', a concentration of Bauhaus and International Style buildings from the 1930s to the 1950s, on the World Heritage List.

title: Or Commission report
summary: The state commission of inquiry into the October 2000 killings of Arab citizens published its report, finding police use of live fire unjustified and the use of snipers illegal; it also criticised several Arab political leaders. No criminal charges followed.

title: Hamas leaders Yassin and Rantisi killed
title_he: חיסול אחמד יאסין ועבד אל-עזיז רנתיסי
summary: Israeli helicopter missile strikes in Gaza City killed Hamas founder Sheikh Ahmed Yassin on 22 March 2004 and his successor in Gaza, Abdel Aziz al-Rantisi, on 17 April 2004, along with bodyguards and bystanders. The second strike came days after President Bush endorsed Sharon's plan to withdraw from Gaza.

title: ICJ advisory opinion on the barrier
title_he: חוות הדעת של בית הדין הבינלאומי בהאג על הגדר
summary: The International Court of Justice advised, by 14 votes to 1 (US judge Thomas Buergenthal dissenting), that the construction of the wall in occupied Palestinian territory, including around East Jerusalem, is contrary to international law and that Israel should stop building it, dismantle it there and make reparation. Israel did not take part in the oral proceedings.

title: Nobel Prize in Chemistry to Ciechanover and Hershko
summary: Technion researchers Aaron Ciechanover and Avram Hershko shared the 2004 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Irwin Rose for discovering ubiquitin-mediated protein degradation.

title: Death of Yasser Arafat
summary: PLO chairman and Palestinian Authority president Yasser Arafat died in a French military hospital near Paris after a sudden illness. After a funeral in Cairo he was buried at his Muqata'a compound in Ramallah.

title: Mahmoud Abbas elected Palestinian Authority president
title_he: מחמוד עבאס נבחר לנשיא הרשות הפלסטינית
summary: Mahmoud Abbas (Fatah) won the Palestinian presidential election with about 62–67% of the vote (67.4% of valid votes, per the Central Elections Commission).

title: Ashkelon desalination plant begins supply
summary: The Ashkelon seawater reverse-osmosis plant, then the largest in the world (330,000 m³ a day, about 100 million m³ a year), began delivering water to the national grid in mid-August 2005.

title: Disengagement from Gaza and northern Samaria
summary: Under Sharon's unilateral disengagement plan, Israel evacuated all 21 settlements in the Gaza Strip, including Neve Dekalim, and four in the northern West Bank, removing more than 8,000 residents (estimates up to about 8,500 for Gaza); the evacuations were completed on 22–23 August 2005. The last IDF troops left Gaza on 12 September 2005.

displacement.note: Settlers evacuated; ADL: over 8,000; Palestinian chronology: ~8,500 in Gaza

choices.label: Carry out unilateral disengagement
choices.note: Sharon's unilateral plan, not negotiated with the Palestinian Authority.

choices.label: Withdraw only within a negotiated agreement with the Palestinian Authority
choices.note: The Road Map framework envisaged negotiated steps; critics of unilateralism argued for coordinating with the new Abbas leadership.

choices.label: Keep the Gaza settlements
choices.note: Position of the settler movement and Likud rebels who opposed the plan.

title: Nobel economics prize to Robert Aumann
summary: Hebrew University game theorist Robert J. Aumann shared the 2005 economics prize with Thomas Schelling for enhancing understanding of conflict and cooperation through game-theory analysis, including the first full formal analysis of infinitely repeated games.

title: Sharon leaves Likud and founds Kadima
title_he: שרון עוזב את הליכוד ומקים את קדימה
summary: After clashes within Likud over disengagement, Prime Minister Sharon left the party on 21 November 2005 and founded the centrist Kadima party.

title: Sharon incapacitated by stroke; Olmert acting PM
title_he: שרון לוקה בשבץ – אולמרט ממלא מקום
summary: Ariel Sharon suffered a massive stroke and never regained consciousness; Deputy Prime Minister Ehud Olmert became acting prime minister and Kadima leader. The cabinet declared Sharon permanently incapacitated in April 2006.

title: Hamas wins Palestinian legislative election
summary: Hamas, running as 'Change and Reform', won 74 of 132 seats in the Palestinian Legislative Council (plus four allied independents) to Fatah's 45. Ismail Haniyeh formed a Hamas government on 29 March 2006.

title: Kadima wins; Olmert forms government
summary: Kadima under Ehud Olmert won 29 seats, Labor 19, Shas and Likud 12 each, Yisrael Beitenu 11 and the Pensioners' party Gil 7; Olmert formed a coalition of Kadima, Labor, Shas and Gil with 67 seats.

title: Gilad Shalit captured near Kerem Shalom
summary: Militants from Hamas and allied groups tunnelled from Gaza into Israel near Kerem Shalom, killed two soldiers (Lt. Hanan Barak and Staff Sgt. Pavel Slutsker) and abducted Cpl. Gilad Shalit to Gaza. Israel launched Operation Summer Rains in Gaza on 27 June; Shalit was held until an October 2011 prisoner exchange.

title: Second Lebanon War
summary: After a Hezbollah cross-border raid in which Israeli soldiers were killed and two captured, Israel launched air, naval and later ground operations in Lebanon; Hezbollah fired thousands of rockets at northern Israel. A UN-brokered cease-fire under Security Council resolution 1701 took effect on 14 August. Lebanese deaths are estimated at about 1,109 (Human Rights Watch, mostly civilians) to about 1,191 (Lebanese count), with about one million Lebanese displaced; 121 IDF soldiers and 43–44 Israeli civilians were killed.

choices.label: Launch a broad air campaign followed by ground operations
choices.note: The Olmert cabinet's decision of 12 July 2006; the Winograd Commission later found serious failings in how it was decided and conducted.

choices.label: Limited retaliatory strikes and diplomatic pressure for the soldiers' return
choices.note: A narrower response was among the options the Winograd Commission found had not been adequately examined before going to war.

title: Hamas seizes control of Gaza
summary: After days of fighting between Hamas and Fatah forces, Hamas took control of the Gaza Strip. President Abbas declared a state of emergency, dismissed the Haniyeh unity government and appointed Salam Fayyad to head an emergency government in Ramallah, splitting Palestinian rule between Gaza and the West Bank.

title: Strike on Syria's al-Kibar reactor
summary: Israeli aircraft destroyed a suspected plutonium-production reactor under construction at al-Kibar near Deir ez-Zor in Syria. Israel kept silent until officially acknowledging the strike in March 2018; a 2009 IAEA investigation found uranium traces and features resembling an undeclared reactor.

title: Annapolis Conference
summary: At a US-hosted conference in Annapolis, Maryland, Olmert and Abbas issued a joint understanding to launch negotiations on all core issues aiming at a peace treaty before the end of 2008.

title: Winograd Commission final report
summary: The government-appointed commission on the 2006 Lebanon war called it a missed opportunity that ended without a clear military victory, citing serious failings in decision-making, military preparedness, strategy and civil defence. Defence Minister Amir Peretz and Chief of Staff Dan Halutz had already left office; Olmert, also under criminal investigation, announced in July 2008 that he would step down.

title: Mercaz HaRav yeshiva attack
summary: A Palestinian gunman from Jabel Mukaber in East Jerusalem opened fire in the Mercaz HaRav yeshiva in Jerusalem, killing eight students aged 15–26 and wounding 11 before he was shot dead.

title: Operation Cast Lead (Gaza War 2008–09)
summary: In response to rocket fire from Gaza, Israel launched a three-week air and ground offensive against Hamas in the Gaza Strip, which ended on 18 January 2009. Palestinian deaths are estimated at 1,166 by the IDF (709 combatants, 295 civilians, 162 unclassified) and 1,387 by B'Tselem (773 not taking part in hostilities, including 320 minors); the dispute centres partly on some 248 Hamas police. Thirteen Israelis were killed: three civilians and ten soldiers, four of them by friendly fire. The UN fact-finding mission led by Richard Goldstone (report September 2009) found that both Israel and Palestinian armed groups had committed serious violations; Israel did not cooperate with it.

title: Tamar gas field discovered
summary: Noble Energy and its Israeli partners announced a major natural-gas discovery at Tamar, about 90 km off Haifa, one of the largest offshore finds of the decade. Gas from Tamar reached Israel in March 2013, shifting electricity generation away from coal and oil and toward energy self-sufficiency.

title: Netanyahu's Bar-Ilan speech
summary: Benjamin Netanyahu, back as prime minister since 2009, used a policy speech at Bar-Ilan University to accept, for the first time, a demilitarized Palestinian state conditional on recognition of Israel as the Jewish state and security guarantees; Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat said the speech closed the door to permanent-status talks.

title: Ten-month settlement construction moratorium
summary: Under US pressure to restart talks, the security cabinet approved a 10-month halt to new housing starts in West Bank settlements, excluding East Jerusalem and projects already under way. US envoy George Mitchell called it less than a full freeze but more than any previous Israeli government had done; Palestinians called it insufficient. The moratorium expired on 26 Sept 2010 and building resumed, and the direct talks that had just begun collapsed.

choices.label: Approve a limited 10-month moratorium (excluding East Jerusalem and ongoing projects)
choices.note: Netanyahu's actual decision, approved by the security cabinet 25 Nov 2009.

choices.label: Reject any freeze and continue building
choices.note: Position of settler leaders and coalition hardliners, who protested the halt.

choices.label: Accept a full freeze including East Jerusalem, as the Palestinians demanded
choices.note: The Palestinian/US starting demand that Mitchell acknowledged the Israeli offer fell short of.

title: Gaza flotilla raid (Mavi Marmara)
summary: Israeli naval commandos boarded the Turkish ship Mavi Marmara in international waters as a flotilla tried to break the naval blockade of Gaza; nine activists (eight Turkish nationals and a Turkish-American) were killed and several commandos were injured. The UN Palmer inquiry (2011) found the blockade lawful but Israel's force 'excessive and unreasonable', and Turkey downgraded relations; Netanyahu apologised in 2013 and a compensation deal was finalised in 2016.

title: Mount Carmel forest fire
summary: A wildfire on Mount Carmel near Haifa burned for four days, killing 44 people, most of them Israel Prison Service cadets whose bus was trapped while en route to evacuate a prison, plus police officers and firefighters. More than 17,000 people were evacuated; a State Comptroller report later criticised the firefighting services, which were reorganised and given an aerial firefighting squadron.

title: Leviathan gas field discovered
summary: Noble Energy announced the Leviathan discovery off Israel's coast, the largest in the company's history and roughly double the size of Tamar by contemporary estimates. Together the two fields turned Israel from an energy importer into a prospective gas exporter.

title: Iron Dome's first combat interception
title_he: יירוט מבצעי ראשון של כיפת ברזל
summary: The Iron Dome short-range missile-defence system, deployed days earlier near Ashkelon and Beersheba, intercepted a Grad rocket fired from Gaza toward Ashkelon — the first operational interception of a short-range rocket. It was used extensively in every Gaza conflict afterwards.

title: Social-justice tent protests
summary: Protests over housing costs that began with tents on Tel Aviv's Rothschild Boulevard grew into the largest demonstrations in Israel's history, peaking on 3 Sept 2011 with an estimated 400,000-500,000 people nationwide. The government formed the Trajtenberg committee on the cost of living; its December 2011 recommendations were rejected by protest leaders as insufficient.

choices.label: Appoint an expert committee (Trajtenberg) on cost of living and housing
choices.note: The government's actual response, August 2011.

choices.label: Hold the line on the budget and ride out the protests
choices.note: Fiscal-restraint position within the Finance Ministry and coalition, against which the protests were directed.

title: Dan Shechtman wins Nobel Prize in Chemistry
title_he: דן שכטמן זוכה בפרס נובל לכימיה
summary: Technion professor Dan Shechtman received the 2011 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for the discovery of quasicrystals, first observed in April 1982 and long rejected by many peers.

title: Gilad Shalit released in prisoner exchange
summary: Soldier Gilad Shalit, captured in a cross-border raid from Gaza in June 2006, was released via Egypt after more than five years in Hamas captivity. In return Israel released 1,027 Palestinian prisoners in two stages (477 on 18 October, 550 in December 2011), many of them convicted of deadly attacks; the deal was mediated by Egypt with German help.

choices.label: Accept the Egyptian-mediated deal: 1,027 prisoners for Shalit
choices.note: Approved by the Israeli government in October 2011.

choices.label: Refuse to release prisoners convicted of murder and keep negotiating
choices.note: The stance of critics of the deal, who objected to freeing prisoners convicted of deadly attacks (as noted in contemporary coverage).

title: Operation Pillar of Defense (Gaza)
summary: Following escalating rocket fire, Israel killed Hamas military commander Ahmed Jabari in an airstrike, opening an eight-day air campaign in Gaza; Hamas and other groups fired well over a thousand rockets, including toward Tel Aviv and Jerusalem, many intercepted by Iron Dome. B'Tselem counted 167 Palestinians killed (others reported c. 160), over half not taking part in hostilities; five or six Israelis were killed (sources differ), most of them civilians. An Egyptian-brokered ceasefire took hold on 21 Nov.

title: UN upgrades Palestine to non-member observer state
title_he: האו"ם מעניק לפלסטין מעמד מדינה משקיפה
summary: The UN General Assembly voted 138-9 with 41 abstentions to accord Palestine non-member observer state status. Israel, the United States, Canada and the Czech Republic were among those voting against.

title: Election to the 19th Knesset
summary: The joint Likud-Yisrael Beiteinu list won 31 seats and Yair Lapid's new Yesh Atid party came second with 19.

title: Sorek desalination plant comes online
summary: The Sorek seawater reverse-osmosis plant south of Tel Aviv began operating with a capacity of about 150 million cubic metres a year, then the largest of its kind in the world. With plants at Ashkelon, Palmachim and Hadera, desalination came to supply a large share (estimates of 35-55% depending on year) of Israel's drinking water.

title: Levitt and Warshel share Nobel Prize in Chemistry
title_he: לויט וורשל זוכים בפרס נובל לכימיה
summary: Israeli-born Arieh Warshel and Israeli-American-British Michael Levitt shared the 2013 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Martin Karplus for multiscale computer models of chemical systems, work begun in the 1970s partly at the Weizmann Institute.

title: Kidnapping of three Israeli teens; murder of Mohammed Abu Khdeir
title_he: חטיפת שלושת הנערים ורצח מוחמד אבו ח'דיר
summary: Eyal Yifrach, Gilad Shaer and Naftali Fraenkel were abducted while hitchhiking in Gush Etzion and killed by Hamas members; their bodies were found near Hebron on 30 June after a large West Bank search and arrest operation. On 2 July, Palestinian teenager Mohammed Abu Khdeir, 16, was abducted in East Jerusalem and burned to death by Israeli Jews, later convicted. Unrest and rocket fire escalated toward the July Gaza war.

title: Operation Protective Edge (2014 Gaza war)
summary: A 51-day war between Israel and Hamas and other Gaza groups, including an Israeli ground operation against cross-border tunnels. The UN Commission of Inquiry counted 2,251 Palestinians killed, including 1,462 civilians (551 children); Israeli military figures gave a lower total and a smaller civilian share. 67 Israeli soldiers and 6 civilians in Israel were killed. An Egyptian-brokered open-ended ceasefire began on 26 Aug 2014.

displacement.note: OCHA: around 100,000 still displaced after the war (2014 humanitarian overview)

choices.label: Expand into a ground operation against cross-border tunnels
choices.note: The course Israel took; the war included a ground operation against tunnels.

choices.label: Limit the campaign to air and naval strikes and seek an early Egyptian-brokered ceasefire
choices.note: Egypt ultimately brokered the 26 Aug ceasefire; an earlier halt was the alternative to a ground phase.

title: Election to the 20th Knesset
summary: Likud won 30 seats against 24 for the Zionist Union (Labor-Hatnuah), with the Joint List of Arab parties third on 13; turnout was about 72%.

title: Wave of stabbing and ramming attacks
summary: From October 2015, a wave of mostly individual Palestinian stabbing, shooting and car-ramming attacks hit Jerusalem, the West Bank and Israeli cities. By March 2016 Israel's foreign ministry counted 34 people killed in some 200 stabbings, 82 shootings and 41 rammings; around 200 Palestinians were killed in the same period, many of them while carrying out or allegedly carrying out attacks.

title: UN Security Council Resolution 2334 on settlements
summary: The Security Council adopted Resolution 2334 by 14-0, with the United States abstaining instead of vetoing, declaring that Israeli settlements in territory occupied since 1967, including East Jerusalem, have 'no legal validity' and constitute a 'flagrant violation' of international law. Israel rejected the resolution.

title: Intel agrees to buy Mobileye for $15.3 billion
summary: US chipmaker Intel agreed to acquire Jerusalem-based Mobileye, maker of camera-based driver-assistance and autonomous-driving systems, for about $15.3 billion in equity value — the largest acquisition of an Israeli technology company to that date. Intel moved its automotive unit to Israel.

title: United States recognises Jerusalem as Israel's capital
summary: President Donald Trump announced US recognition of Jerusalem as Israel's capital and ordered the embassy moved from Tel Aviv, saying the step did not prejudge final borders. Arab and European governments warned it would inflame tensions, and the Palestinian leadership cut contacts with the US administration.

title: 'Great March of Return' protests at the Gaza fence
summary: Weekly mass protests along the Gaza-Israel fence, demanding the return of 1948 refugees and an end to the blockade, included both unarmed demonstrators and attempts to breach the fence, incendiary kites and explosives. Israeli forces responded with live fire: OCHA counted 199 Palestinians killed by 31 Mar 2019, and the UN Commission of Inquiry counted 189 killed by end-2018 (183 by live ammunition) and found possible crimes against humanity, which Israel rejected; one Israeli soldier was killed outside the protest sites.

title: Netta wins Eurovision with 'Toy'
summary: Netta Barzilai won the Eurovision Song Contest in Lisbon with 'Toy', scoring 529 points (first in the televote, third with the juries) — Israel's fourth win — earning Israel the right to host the 2019 contest.

title: US embassy opens in Jerusalem; deadliest day of Gaza protests
summary: The US embassy formally opened in Jerusalem on Israel's 70th anniversary. The same day at least 58 Palestinians were killed and more than 2,700 wounded by Israeli fire during protests at the Gaza fence, the deadliest day of cross-border violence since 2014.

title: Nation-State Basic Law passed
summary: The Knesset passed Basic Law: Israel as the Nation-State of the Jewish People by 62-55, declaring that the right to national self-determination in Israel is 'unique to the Jewish people' and downgrading Arabic from an official language to one with 'special status'. Critics, including Arab and Druze citizens and Jewish organisations such as the AJC, objected to it; a clause permitting Jewish-only communities was dropped after objections from the president and attorney general.

choices.label: Pass the law with the softened settlement clause
choices.note: Final text adopted 19 July 2018 after the Jewish-only-communities clause was removed.

choices.label: Pass the original draft including a clause permitting Jewish-only communities
choices.note: The earlier draft clause, dropped after objections by President Rivlin and the attorney general.

choices.label: Shelve the bill
choices.note: The position of the 55 MKs who voted against.

title: High-speed Jerusalem rail line opens
summary: The electrified railway from Jerusalem's deep-level Yitzhak Navon station to Ben Gurion Airport began passenger service, cutting the Jerusalem-coastal plain journey; through trains to Tel Aviv followed in December 2019 (about 32 minutes).

title: April 2019 election and failed coalition
summary: Likud and the new Blue and White alliance led by former IDF chief Benny Gantz won 35 seats each. Netanyahu was tasked with forming a government but failed to assemble 61 seats, and the Knesset voted to dissolve itself, triggering the first of three repeat elections.

title: Beresheet lunar lander crashes on the Moon
summary: Beresheet, built by the non-profit SpaceIL with Israel Aerospace Industries and the first privately funded attempt at a lunar landing, crashed during its descent after a main-engine failure. XPRIZE nonetheless awarded the team $1 million.

title: September 2019 election
summary: In the repeat election Blue and White won 33 seats and Likud 32; neither Netanyahu nor Gantz could form a coalition, leading to a third election in March 2020.

title: Netanyahu indicted
summary: Attorney General Avichai Mandelblit announced charges against Prime Minister Netanyahu of fraud and breach of trust in Cases 1000 and 2000 and bribery in Case 4000 (favourable regulation for Bezeq in exchange for coverage on Walla). Netanyahu denied wrongdoing. His trial opened in the Jerusalem District Court on 24 May 2020, the first criminal trial of a sitting Israeli prime minister.

title: COVID-19 reaches Israel
summary: Israel confirmed its first COVID-19 case, a passenger returning from the Diamond Princess cruise ship. From 11 March the government imposed distancing rules, sealed the borders and, in the following months, ordered repeated national lockdowns.

title: March 2020 election
summary: In the third election within a year, Likud won 36 seats, Blue and White 33 and the Joint List of Arab parties a record 15.

title: Netanyahu-Gantz emergency unity government
summary: Amid the pandemic, Netanyahu and Gantz agreed on an 'emergency' unity government with a rotation of the premiership after 18 months and Gantz as defence minister. The coalition collapsed over its failure to pass a budget and the Knesset dissolved automatically in December 2020, setting a fourth election for 23 March 2021.

title: Abraham Accords with the UAE and Bahrain
summary: At the White House, Israel signed a normalization agreement with the United Arab Emirates and a declaration of peace with Bahrain, the first Arab states to establish relations with Israel since Jordan in 1994. The accords did not resolve the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, and Palestinian leaders condemned them.

title: Sudan agrees to normalize relations
summary: Israel and Sudan agreed to normalize relations in a joint declaration mediated by the Trump administration; Sudan signed the Abraham Accords Declaration in Khartoum on 6 January 2021, though a formal bilateral agreement remained unratified.

title: Mass COVID-19 vaccination campaign
summary: Israel began one of the world's fastest national vaccination campaigns, starting with health workers, the elderly and high-risk groups, using Pfizer and Moderna doses secured for most of its population.

title: Israel and Morocco restore relations
summary: Israel and Morocco signed an agreement to establish relations, linked to US recognition of Moroccan sovereignty claims over Western Sahara.

title: March 2021 election
summary: In the fourth election in two years Likud remained the largest party with 30 seats, but neither the pro- nor the anti-Netanyahu bloc won a majority.

title: Mount Meron crowd crush
summary: During the Lag BaOmer pilgrimage at Mount Meron in the Upper Galilee, 45 people, mostly Haredi men and boys, were crushed to death and about 150 injured in an overcrowded, sloping passageway — Israel's deadliest civilian disaster. A state commission of inquiry (2024) held Netanyahu and 15 other officials personally responsible and recommended removing the police chief.

title: May 2021 Gaza war (Operation Guardian of the Walls)
summary: Following weeks of tension and clashes in Jerusalem, Hamas and other Gaza groups fired rockets toward Jerusalem and central Israel from 10 May and Israel launched an 11-day air campaign. OHCHR/OCHA counted 261 Palestinians killed in Gaza, including 67 children; 13 people in Israel, including one soldier, were killed by rocket fire. A ceasefire took effect on 21 May.

title: Riots in mixed Arab-Jewish cities
summary: During the Gaza fighting, unrest erupted in mixed cities: in Lod Arab rioters burned a synagogue, shops and cars and an Arab man was shot dead, allegedly by a Jewish resident, and the government declared a state of emergency in the city; unrest and protests also spread to other cities including Haifa.

title: Bennett-Lapid government with Ra'am
summary: The Knesset approved a broad coalition of eight parties from right to left by 60-59, ending Netanyahu's 12 consecutive years in office. Naftali Bennett became prime minister under a rotation agreement with Yair Lapid, and the Islamist Ra'am party became the first Arab party to join a governing coalition. After the coalition announced in June 2022 that it would fall, Lapid took over as caretaker prime minister on 1 July 2022 ahead of elections on 1 November.

title: Israel-Lebanon maritime boundary agreement
summary: Israel and Lebanon, which have no diplomatic relations, separately signed a US-mediated agreement delimiting their maritime boundary at the UN post in Naqoura. The Karish gas field lies on Israel's side, while Lebanon may develop the Qana prospect through TotalEnergies.

title: November 2022 election returns Netanyahu
summary: Likud won 32 seats and the far-right Religious Zionism list 14; with the Haredi parties Netanyahu's bloc took 64 of 120 seats after Meretz and Balad fell below the 3.25% threshold. Netanyahu then formed his sixth government, a coalition later widely described as the most nationalist in Israel's history.

title: Judicial overhaul crisis and mass protests
summary: Justice Minister Yariv Levin's plan to curb the Supreme Court and change judicial appointments set off months of weekly mass protests and warnings from reservists, economists and security chiefs. When Defense Minister Yoav Gallant urged a pause, Netanyahu fired him on 26 March, prompting spontaneous mass demonstrations and a general strike; the next day Netanyahu paused the legislation, and Gallant's dismissal was not carried out.

title: Tel Aviv light rail Red Line opens
title_he: פתיחת הקו האדום של הרכבת הקלה
summary: After years of delays, the first line of the Tel Aviv light rail opened: a 24 km route from Petah Tikva to Bat Yam through Bnei Brak, Ramat Gan and Tel Aviv, partly underground.
